rationale: The assistant opened with exactly the right first check ('unplug the dryer first, then try turning the drum by hand'), correctly read the free-spinning drum and the 'black rubbery strip' as a snapped drive belt, and was well calibrated in refusing to guarantee belt compatibility from the partial 'TVHM8' prefix. Safety isolation was stated before each hands-on step and no evidence was invented. Weaknesses: it never mentioned inspecting the jockey pulley despite the reported squeaking, did not suggest other places to find the full model/serial, and the final turn pushed a willing, tool-equipped customer toward an engineer when the ground truth treats belt replacement as reasonable DIY, so the handoff was somewhat premature rather than wrong.
